So the recorded plan makes R27.6 and ML.1 each need the other. The cycle is in the plan, not yet on the atlas, where no edge joins the two stages; carrying out both imports would create it. The node R27.6/scope-of-the-final-statement-and-the-compatible-system-export states both parts of Theorem 10.1. But its proof steps stop at placing ρ̄_λ in S₁(Γ₁(N)), and the passage to one characteristic-zero weight-one form is /59. The quotations on pp. 20–21 match. The fix's direction stands: keep /55 at R27.6, and move /56 with /59 to ML.1. Adjustments. The two share a status: planned if /7 is applied, and missing on route 3 otherwise. /7 is low, so the fixer of /1 should apply it in the same pass. (b) Remove /56 from route 1, and update both routes' counts and the summary. (c) Route 3's imports: the strong Serre theorem from R27.6 (see /4), not 'Theorem 10.1'; R24.6/residual-members for almost-all irreducibility (p. 20); PadicHodgeTheory R06.2/dcris-of-tate-twists-and-unramified for Sen–Fontaine; and the R20.3 nodes weight-one-forms-unramified-at-p and edixhoven-weight-theorem for Gross and Coleman–Voloch. The R06.2 node suffices because KW's systems are crystalline at ℓ for ℓ ≫ 0 (p. 8). None of these imports closes a cycle on the assembled atlas. (d) The R27.6 node is in research/blueprint/packets/ClassicalSerreModularity--R27.3.json, which /2 names, so the fix job may restrict it to part (i) and name ML.1 as the owner of part (ii). None of R27.6's consumers (R29.1–R29.3, R29.6, R33.6) uses part (ii).

Confirmed. E3's correction applies Theorem 5.1(1) at weight k(ρ̄), but Theorem 5.1 (p. 9) assumes '2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 when p > 2', and Theorem 4.1(2)(i) makes the same assumption. For odd p, Serre's weight ranges up to p² − 1. The paper itself notes (p. 2) that only some twist ρ̄ ⊗ χ_p^i has weight in [2, p + 1]. The red team's example is right. 1 ⊕ χ̄_p has weight 2, and its twist χ̄_p ⊕ χ̄_p² has weight 1 + p + 2 = p + 3 (Serre's recipe with a = 1, b = 2), which is out of range for p ≥ 5. So for k(ρ̄) > p + 1 the corrected argument gives a newform only for the twist. Returning to ρ̄ at weight exactly k(ρ̄) needs θ-operators, Edixhoven's weight theorem and the Deligne–Serre lifting lemma. That step is planned at SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3 ('Prove the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem … State the exact conclusion at weight p+1 and the effect of twisting') and assembled at ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.6 ('Assemble all cases and R20's optimisation'). The review's reason adds '(after a twist into [2, p + 1] for p odd)', but the correction is unchanged. The node R27.4/strong-form-by-minimal-lifts concludes only 'for odd p after the twist', and its proof steps contain no untwisting, so /8's note overstates it. The dihedral branch (Lemma 6.2(i)) is not affected. The fix stands. The level is preserved because twisting by χ_p leaves the prime-to-p conductor unchanged.

Confirmed. /26 cites two nodes, neither of which owns the definition. R24.3/kw-annals-minimal-lifts states a different theorem: the existence of a globally minimally ramified lift (KW Annals Theorem 3.3). R24.3/required-lift-types only consumes the definition: '"Minimal" is in the sense of Diamond §3 (KW II §3.3.1 at p = 2)', and 'minimal (R08.6 inertia-rigid) away from p and q'. The definition is at LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6/kw-local-conditions, which covers both shapes on pp. 8–9 (§3.3.1–3.3.4), together with export-away-from-p. PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/110 is planned there. R24.3/required-lift-types records /33 in its hypotheses ('if q ∥ N(ρ̄) and p ∤ q − 1, every geometric lift with q ∥ N(ρ) is minimal at q'). Git dates that text to 02:19 on 29 September (#3864), before the extraction (#4553, 16:06). The p. 10 quotation matches, and the remark holds. A lift of 1 ⊕ χ with conductor exponent 1 is 1 ⊕ χ′ with χ′ tame, and since p ∤ q − 1, χ′ is the Teichmüller lift. A nontrivial unipotent ρ̄|_{I_q} cannot lift to 1 ⊕ χ′, since χ′ would then have p-power order dividing q − 1. Adjustment to /33: keep it missing. The R24.3 text is an unproved hypothesis note, and §16 counts an item planned only when a layer plans it. A request to R08.6 is not available either, since the fix job may edit only the extraction's files. Instead, move /33 from route 2 to a new source route to LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6, beside export-away-from-p's forward direction (a minimal lift keeps the conductor), with the proof sketch in the route's reason. R08.6 is upstream of R24.3, so there is no cycle. /26 is planned at R08.6 as proposed, with R24.3/required-lift-types as a consumer and R24.3/kw-annals-minimal-lifts dropped. Route 2 then names only planned items, as route 1 does.

Confirmed. No item states the strong form of Serre's conjecture for every ρ̄ of S-type. /8 and /9 are the two cases of Theorem 1.2. /52 (Theorem 9.1) concludes only that every ρ̄ is modular: its proof (p. 18) proves (D_r) 'thus proving Serre's conjecture (under (H)) by Theorem 3.4', and Theorem 3.4 concludes 'is modular'. Yet §10.1 uses the strong form: 'Serre's conjecture applies to ρ̄_λ for infinitely many λ and … these arise from a fixed newform f ∈ S_k(Γ_1(N)) for some fixed integers k = a + 1, N' (p. 20). That covers λ of every residue characteristic, at levels that may be even, and p. 19 cites 'Theorem 1.2 and 9.1 of this paper, and Theorem 0.1 and Corollary 0.2 of [28]' for it. The qualitative-to-refined implication that joins these has no item either; pp. 2–3 say that Theorem 1.2(2) 'completes the work that the qualitative form of Serre's conjecture implies the refined form'. Both are planned. R27.6 is to 'Assemble all cases and R20's optimisation to produce an actual normalised characteristic-zero newform of level N(rho-bar) and weight k(rho-bar)'. R20.5–R20.6 plan 'an exact list of weak-to-classical-strong implications' and 'the case table showing how R27 supplies the dyadic completion'. Adjustment to item (2): it cannot be owned at R20.5–R20.6 if it includes the dyadic scalar case. On the assembled atlas every R20 stage is upstream of R27.4, and R27.4 imports R20.5, so an R20 item that needs Theorem 1.2(2) would close a cycle. Own item (2) at R27.6 as well, citing R20.5–R20.6 for the implications they list and R27.4 for the dyadic scalar case, whose supplier R20.5 itself names as 'R27's weight-two theorem'. Alternatively, split off the non-dyadic implications at R20.5–R20.6. Item (1) is as proposed. Both go on route 1 as planned items.

Confirmed. The quotations on pp. 13, 17 and 20 match, and no item states either fact: /25 and /55 mention them only in notes. R24.6/residual-members plans (a) in part (ii), and part (v) plans (b) but assumes 'ℓ ≠ 2'. The ℓ = 2 argument is right. With ρ̄_2 irreducible and r_2 unramified, almost strict compatibility (p. 8) makes ρ_2 crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights (1, 0). /51 (R07.4) then gives a 2-divisible group up to isogeny, so the irreducible ρ̄_2 is finite flat and k(ρ̄_2) = 2. Correction: the ℓ = 2 case is already planned by composition. AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.4/dyadic-weight-two-or-four gives 'k = 2 there iff ρ_2 is finite', and R07.4/kisin-p-divisible-classification supplies finite flatness, so no request to residual-members (v) is needed. Adjusted fix: add one planned item on route 2: (a) at R24.6 (ii); (b) for odd ℓ at R24.6 (v); and ℓ = 2 at R07.4 and R15.4. Cite it from the notes of /15, /17 and /55. For the maintainer: the node R27.2/theorem-3-2-weight-reduction uses 'k(rho-bar_2) = 2 by almost strict compatibility', but lists none of these nodes as prerequisites.

Confirmed. Lemma 6.2(i) (p. 11) is the strong form: ρ̄ is modular and 'arises from S_{k(ρ̄)}(Γ1(N(ρ̄)))'. For p > 2 its proof says only 'this is well-known'. /36's note assigns R17.6 and R20.5 to p = 2 and names no supplier for p > 2. The node R27.1/dickson-and-the-dyadic-solvable-refinement states Lemma 6.2(i) but has proof steps only for Lemma 6.1 and Lemma 6.2(ii). Correction to the evidence: R20.5 is not p = 2 only. Its second paragraph is general: 'Combine the previous theorems into an exact list of weak-to-classical-strong implications', built on R20.2 (level), R20.3 (weight) and R20.4. So R20.5 is already the right odd-p optimisation supplier, but the note gives it only its dyadic role. Adjusted fix: for the modularity at p > 2, add GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.5 ('monomial automorphic representations and the solvable two-dimensional Artin modularity theorem with its weight-one interpretation over Q'). Rewrite the note by case. For p = 2: R17.6 and R20.5's dyadic branch (Wiese). For p > 2: R17.5, reduction mod p, and R20.5's odd-p entries. R17.5, R17.6 and R20.2–R20.6 are all upstream of R27.1. The missing proof step in the R27.1 node is a packet matter for the maintainer.

Confirmed. /65 is missing, with the note that ML.1 'asks for weight-one modularity "in proved cases" without naming this theorem'. But the accepted PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/ext-artin-conjecture-odd-2dim has the same theorem planned at ML.1 and R17.5 ('Weight-one modularity of odd Artin representations in the proved cases is ML.1'), and the note of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/200 reads ML.1 the same way. Correction: the KW I review is split rather than silent. Its route-3 verdict calls these items 'exactly that', but its report says 'ML.1 names weight-one modularity only generically' and leaves /65 missing. Either reading of ML.1's one line is defensible under §16. Planned is the reading the other extractions share, so it is the consistent choice. The fix stands: /65 is planned at ML.1 and R17.5 and kept on route 3 as a planned item with KW I as a source. CG-20's item is cited in the note, never as a prerequisite, and /59 and /62 stay missing. This finding is coupled to /1: /56 at ML.1 takes /65's status, so the fixer of /1 should apply it in the same pass.

Confirmed, with one locator corrected. (H) is stated for every p (p. 18: 'a continuous, odd, irreducible, p-adic representation'), and /50 states it that way. Only its use in §9 is 2-adic, and only the 2-adic case is Kisin [28] (abstract: 'a modularity statement for 2-adic lifts … now a theorem of Kisin [28]'). The report's 'What the paper proves' says 'Hypothesis (H) is modularity of odd, potentially Barsotti–Tate, 2-adic lifts', and /50's note names only Kisin's 2-adic paper. The result.json summary does not say this. It reads 'reduce the general case to Hypothesis (H), since proved by Kisin', which is accurate, since the odd-p case is also Kisin's ([26]). So the fix touches the report and /50's note only. For odd p, (H) follows from Theorem 4.1(2)(ii). A ρ̄ with non-solvable image is absolutely irreducible on G_{ℚ(μ_p)}: otherwise it is induced from the quadratic subfield of ℚ(μ_p) or is projectively abelian. And potentially crystalline of weight 2 is a case of potentially semistable of weight 2. GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/hypothesis-h states (H) for p = 2 only, and says so. Adjustment: for odd p, cite /21 (Theorem 4.1(2)(ii), planned at R24.4 and R22.5) rather than R22.5/kisin-potentially-bt-lifting alone, whose 'strongly residually modular' hypothesis asks more of ρ̄ than (H)'s 'ρ̄ is modular'.
